name: India–Pakistan
value: Indus treaty in abeyance; no LoC strike
summary: Pakistan tells the UN India's Indus treaty suspension is unlawful; no cross-border strike or mobilisation found
state: At the UN Security Council on 18 Nov Pakistan called India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty, in abeyance since April 2025, outlaw behaviour, citing an August arbitration award that found the treaty still in force (Dawn, 19 Nov). Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian aircraft, in place since April 2025, was last notified to run to 23 Nov; any renewal was not confirmed (Airways Magazine). No cross-border strike or mobilisation was found to 24 Nov, so Watch holds on the treaty suspension.
for_you: Check FCDO travel advice before travel near the Line of Control or the India–Pakistan border, where the FCDO advises against travel to some areas. Indian aircraft have been barred from Pakistani airspace, which lengthens some routes.
rubric_hit: Watch: treaty suspension (Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance since Apr 2025); no cross-border strikes

sources.title: Dawn — India's move on Indus Waters Treaty is 'outlaw behaviour', Pakistan tells UN
Airways Magazine — Pakistan extends Indian aircraft airspace ban until November 24

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
